title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction & spillover memory manager to reduce fragmentation and paging
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory management: adaptive eviction, background compaction, spillover to NVMe, and new metrics; reduces OOM/fragmentation and tail paging.
description:
Motivation: Production clusters running mixed-length chat workloads observed increased KV cache fragmentation and NVMe paging during sustained high-concurrency workloads. This caused intermittent OOMs on nodes and higher p50/p99 token latencies due to background paging. This PR implements an adaptive memory manager for the KV cache that reduces fragmentation, delays/predicts paging, and performs controlled background spillover/compaction to improve stability and tail latency.

What changed (summary): Implemented a new KVCacheMemoryManager that: (1) maintains allocation slabs per-size-class to avoid internal fragmentation; (2) tracks hotness via a lightweight epoch-based LRU and promotes frequently-accessed KV entries to a hot tier; (3) introduces an async background compaction pass that coalesces small free fragments when memory pressure is detected; (4) implements an adaptive spillover policy that writes low-hotness shards to local NVMe using a compact on-disk layout and rehydrates on access; (5) exposes tunable thresholds (mem_high, mem_target, mem_low, compaction_window_ms, spillover_rate_limit) and integrates with the request scheduler to throttle eviction/compaction during latency-sensitive periods.

Key heuristics: - Sequence-aware eviction: prefer evicting long-sequence prefixes when they yield low reuse probability; keep short-sequence KV for latency-critical short prompt workloads. - Hotness scoring: combination of recency counter and access frequency sampled via epoch ticks to avoid noisy counters on very-high-throughput paths. - Compaction trigger: compaction runs when free memory < mem_high and free_frag_bytes > fragmentation_threshold OR when continuous paging observed for > 5s. - Spillover policy: spill least-hot shard-first, cap spill bandwidth to avoid NVMe saturation; rehydrate on demand with async prefetch for predicted next-token continuation.

APIs and config: Added new fields to the runtime config: kv_cache.memory_manager.mode (off|adaptive), kv_cache.memory_manager.mem_high/target/low, kv_cache.memory_manager.compaction_window_ms, kv_cache.memory_manager.spillover_enabled, kv_cache.memory_manager.spillover_bandwidth_bytes_per_sec. Defaults chosen to be conservative for existing deployments (mode=adaptive, mem_high=0.92, mem_target=0.8, mem_low=0.6).

Performance and metrics: - Canary perf tests on perf-canary region (mixed 8k/512 workloads) show: 12% reduction in OOMs during 6h soak, 8% improvement in p99 token latency, and 20% reduction in NVMe read/write bytes attributed to paging. - Microbench: compaction pass costs ~0.3ms per GC-frame under typical load; spillback latency for cold rehydrates ~4-8ms (dominant NVMe seek). Metrics added: kv_cache.compaction_runs, kv_cache.spillover_bytes, kv_cache.hot_promotion_rate, kv_cache.fragmentation_ratio.

Testing: unit tests for allocator, hotness promotion/demotion, spill/rehydration logic; integration tests in redwood-quickstarts; e2e stress in perf-canary with continuous-batching enabled. Observed one flaky test (test_kv_spill_rehydrate) that failed in a matrix run due to timing nondeterminism; added stronger synchronization and retry in that test.

Rollout plan: - Merge behind kill-switch flag (kv_cache.memory_manager.mode) defaulting to adaptive for new clusters; - Canary rollout to perf-canary and two internal high-concurrency clusters for 72h; - Warn and auto-roll back if kv_cache.spillover_bytes or compaction_runs exceed heuristics or if p99 token latency regresses >5%.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Canary perf runs - [x] Docs updated (config guide) - [x] Metrics and dashboards added - [x] Feature gated with runtime flag

Notes: This is a follow-up to ENG-4211 and builds on the prior spillover work (pr-110812, pr-116432). The implementation keeps the public API unchanged and is non-breaking.

Detailed diff summary: see changed_files for specific touched modules (kv_cache allocator, memory_manager, disk_spill, scheduler integration, config, tests, docs).

merge_commit_message:
kv-cache: adaptive eviction & spillover memory manager to reduce fragmentation and paging

Implements slab allocator, background compaction, NVMe spillover, scheduler integration, and metrics. Canary-tested and feature-gated.
notes: Backported config knobs to release/2024.11 for targeted customers. Monitoring dashboards added under observability -> kv_cache. No public API changes.
